target_3_burn_conversion_gate_verdict.verdict: REFUTED AS WRITTEN. The falsifier's first clause is satisfied literally and unambiguously on 0709: a CDD add, burn-confirmed on both limbs (level flat-to-up, wind not ramping), that not merely failed to deliver but produced the worst down day of the block. I am recording this as a refutation and not softening it into 'mis-scoped', because the gate's own falsifier was written to catch exactly this and it caught it.
target_3_burn_conversion_gate_verdict.the_mechanism_behind_the_refutation_whic: The gate's CDD-ADD LIMB IS A CONSTANT, AND A CONSTANT CANNOT GATE. Measured across every day of G22 and G23 on the same S110-grafted ladder (n=20): d_gw_cdd at horizon 1 is POSITIVE 20/20 (min +0.129, max +2.256); the near limb h0+h1 is positive 19/20 (min -0.357, max +2.073, median +1.115). The near-horizon CDD run-delta never changes sign - it is a model-cycle artifact (each successive run raises the D+1 CDD as the target resolves), not a demand signal. So the gate, fed the near horizons, licenses an up-lean EVERY SINGLE DAY and can never decline. Whatever discriminating work the gate did on its G22 evidence was done by the WIND/BURN limbs, not by the CDD-add limb, which was on all ten of those days too. Compounding this: grid_stack is D+2 stale BY CONSTRUCTION (0709 reads period 2026-07-07), so the burn confirmation is BACKWARD-LOOKING - it can only ever confirm that a load already in the past converted to gas call. It is structurally incapable of confirming a FORWARD add, which is the only add the front month prices.
target_3_burn_conversion_gate_verdict.the_repair_proposed_not_merged: HORIZON-SCOPE THE GATE. The burn limb is a CONVERSION test (did load become gas call) and is sound as such; it is being applied to the wrong quantity. Take the slope on the FORWARD ladder (h>=2), which does vary sign (9/20 positive over the same 20 days, median -0.442), and never on h0/h1. Re-state burn's role as a conversion CHECK on that forward add's plausibility, explicitly labelled as evidence about the past.
target_3_burn_conversion_gate_verdict.the_repair_is_NOT_a_new_direction_rule_a: I ran the obvious follow-up honestly and it fails. Forward-limb sign vs day-move sign over the same 20 days: G22 4 agree / 5 disagree / 1 flat; G23 6 agree / 3 disagree / 1 tie-ish - about 10/19, a coin flip. The single most POSITIVE forward limb of all 20 days (0715, +5.859) delivered -60. The forward-ladder integral does NOT sort direction and I make no such claim. Its only defensible use on the measured record is as a MAGNITUDE-PERMISSION descriptor at a record extreme AND ONLY WHEN INDEPENDENT CHANNELS AGREE - on 0709 the forward limb was the most negative of the 20 (-3.601) with roll, STEO and the surplus all same-signed; on 0715 it was the most positive with the tape mid-block basing and nothing else aligned. That discriminator has n=1 clean and I flag it BELOW the n>=2 bar rather than dress it up.
target_3_burn_conversion_gate_verdict.attribution_fence: The gate was merged S110 and the ladder was grafted S110, so the gate has never been evaluated on an unrepaired input; both G22 and G23 states carry the identical graft from the identical store via the identical assembly with the identical two identity proofs, so my near/forward split compares like with like across groups. I do NOT re-attribute the gate's own G22 quantities: its '0629 realized +4.8 CDD add' equals none of my measured limbs for that day (near +0.919 / fwd +4.275 / sum +5.194), so it is stated in a different unit and the gate's G22 record stands untouched. I claim only that the limb AS WRITTEN, evaluated on the ladder AS SERVED, cannot decline.

clears_the_bar.claim: On EIA print Thursdays the session's NET SIGNED FLOW does not sort the day's sign - it anti-sorts it. Measured per-event across G17-G23: sign(day net) == sign(session signed flow) on 4 of 13 print Thursdays (0416, 0514, 0521, 0611 agree; 0423, 0430, 0507, 0528, 0604, 0618, 0625, 0709, 0716 disagree). clears_the_bar.mechanism: The 10:30 release forces two-sided aggression into one window.
